about: Local state scenarios on a real filesystem (appendix A 14, 31, 34 and the plan's protection, limit, deadline and tab contracts). Each scenario states the starting files, the action, and what must hold afterwards. Contexts are the query identity a file or handle is bound to (command, target, sort or tab, filters, normalized window, the X account id). All state lives under the skill's data/ directory (TWITTER_DATA_DIR in tests). source: threads (the store is ported from the threads skill), code (the previous twitter skill), plan.

collection.fact: --out writes NDJSON: a header line (kind header, format 3, the query context, started_at), then records, each page closed by a kind:page marker (cursor state, ids, n, stop_reason, reply coverage when a post's replies are collected). Only complete pages are trusted: on resume the tail after the last marker is dropped and re-read. A file for another query or account, an older format or the previous twitter skill's format is refused before any byte changes. A marker whose ids or n disagree with the records above it is an integrity failure. The file is opened without following a symlink, mode 0600, locked without waiting; writes are fsynced. A file whose last marker says the surface ended (exhausted or window_reached) is complete and requests nothing. A path inside the skill's data/ is refused.

handles.fact: A handle is a monotonically increasing number bound to its query context and the X account. The counter reservation is fsynced before the handle file is written, so a crash leaves a gap, never a reused number; the counter is never deleted or lowered. Handles expire after 24 hours and are cleaned up by the skill itself (the model is never told to delete them). Files are 0600 in a 0700 directory. Handle files carry format 3. The previous twitter skill's handles (six lowercase letters or digits, kept under ~/.cache) are not numbers and are refused before any file is touched.

protection.fact: Protection state is written atomically (temporary file, fsync, replace) under data/protection/. State that cannot be read counts as blocked (fail closed). A lock or challenge blocks every request until a person clears it and doctor --unblock verifies it; the block records the X account id when it is known (empty when it was seen before the account was known). Per-operation buckets live beside it; a bucket at 0 refuses only its operation until reset; an operation's 429 is never an account block and never downgrades or replaces one. Check block -> check the operation's bucket -> check the command's cap -> pace -> request -> classify -> record block and bucket all happen under one cross-process lock; lock waiting counts against the command's deadline. Every charged request and every unwatched count is appended to an observation log (time, kind, n, operation) kept for 24 hours; the log is never enforced.

unblock.fact: doctor --unblock clears a person-cleared block only after one verification read: a Viewer query sent through a slot that passes the person block alone (Viewer's bucket, pacing and the deadline still apply). It clears only when the answer is 200 with data, the account id in it equals the store's session.user_id, and the block's account id is empty or the same — then the block is removed inside the same critical section. Every failure keeps the block and exits 5 with verification_reason (rate_limited, logged_out, account_mismatch, moved, time_limit, aside); 'other commands work' is never said there. Success clears the person block only; buckets are kept.

tab_protection.fact: The dedicated tab classifies the app's own /i/api/ responses (a hook installed once per page load) and keeps what it saw, with the time, in that tab's sessionStorage (survives a reload of the same tab, not a lost tab). Every call reads that record and the tab's location before sending anything, turns a lock, challenge or /account/access move into a block and a 429 into that operation's bucket, and only then clears the record. A call that records a block blanks the tab to about:blank (no request). A newly opened tab is checked (location, document markers, store session) before any query. The skill's own direct requests are not seen by the hook (they use the fetch the page had before the hook was installed).

session.fact: One dedicated x.com tab per Aside account, recorded by targetId in data/session/<account>.json together with the use token and the operations learned there. Find, re-check, open and record happen under one session lock, so concurrent starts open one tab. Only a targetId the skill recorded is its tab; a tab found by URL is never adopted. A corrupt session file reopens a tab once and says so. A learned value is saved only after the command's read with it was verified.
